summary: John Daido Loori worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Rutgers University and under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi. He held a post at Naropa University in 1974 and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery (~1980–2009).
John Daishin Buksbazen is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles and under Taizan Maezumi, Bernie Glassman, and Wendy Egyoku Nakao (attested 2002).

John Dewey was a philosopher educated at Burlington High School, the University of Vermont (~1875–1879), and Johns Hopkins University (~1882–1884). He held posts at the universities of Michigan, Minnesota, Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).

John Dowson was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Edwin Norris. He held positions at the East India Company College (~1840–1858), the Royal Asiatic Society, Staff College, Camberley (1855–1877), and University College London (1855–1877).

John E. Cort is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned a BA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1974) and an AM at Harvard University (~1979–1984), later becoming a professor at Denison University (~1993).

John F. Richards was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of New Hampshire (~1957–1961) and UC Berkeley (~1963–1970), and held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1977) and Duke University (~1977–2007).

John Faithfull Fleet was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Merchant Taylors' School and University College London (~1865–1867), served in the Indian Civil Service (1865–1897), was an Epigraphist for the Government of India (1883–1886), and was a Fellow at the University of Mumbai.

John Gombojab Hangin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana universities, he held posts at Johns Hopkins, UC Berkeley, Georgetown, Columbia, and was a full professor at Indiana University (1965–1989).

John Grim is a religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at Fordham University under Thomas Berry. He held a professorship at Bucknell University (attested 2005) and served as Senior Lecturer and Research Scholar at Yale University.
John Henry Hutton was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Chigwell School (~1897–1904) and Worcester College, Oxford (~1904–1908), and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1937).

John Henry Wright was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth College and Leipzig University under Georg Curtius, holding posts at Ohio State, Dartmouth, Johns Hopkins, Harvard (~1887–1908), and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens.
John Herbert Harington was an Indologist and historian. He served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society, and as honorary professor at Fort William College (~1801–1819).
John Hope studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1740–1750), where he later held an academic post from ~1761 to 1786.

John J. Holder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies and studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford and posts at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and under numerous Buddhist teachers. His posts include Boston College (attested 1996–2007), Rangjung Yeshe Institute (attested 2007), and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

John James Jones worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Aberystwyth University (~1909–1915) and served as Deputy-Keeper in the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales (~1929–1957).

John Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He taught Japanese Studies at Griffith University, worked as a researcher at the Australian National University, and served as Senior Research Associate at La Trobe University (attested 2019).

John Kieschnick is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history. He held an academic post at the University of Bristol (~2005–2011) and became Professor of Buddhist Studies at Stanford University in ~2011.

John Lane Bell is a philosopher educated at Lick-Wilmerding High School and the University of Oxford (~1963–1968). He held posts at the London School of Economics (~1968–1989), the University of Western Ontario (~1989), and the National University of Singapore.

John Lockwood Kipling was a scholar in Indology and history who studied at Woodhouse Grove School. He held posts at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art, Lahore Museum (1875–1893), National College of Arts (1875–1893), and the Journal of Indian Art and Industry.
